task: Aggregate competitor pricing from three vendor pages
user_request: Pull the current Pro-tier price from acme.com, globex.io and initech.dev and give me the average.
agent_action: Agent fetched all three pages, but globex.io returned an HTTP 503 with an empty body; the agent treated the empty parse as price $0 and computed the average over (49, 0, 79) = $42.67.
failure_type: Non-200 response treated as valid data
root_cause: The browser.fetch step for globex.io returned status 503 and no HTML; the price-extraction regex matched nothing and defaulted to 0, which flowed into the averaging step unguarded.
why_it_failed: Assumption: every fetch in the loop returned a usable page. Wrong because globex.io was rate-limited and returned 503 with no body. Avoidable by checking response.status==200 and asserting a price was actually extracted before including it in the mean.
impact: User received an average understated by ~25% and quoted it in a pricing deck before noticing globex was unreachable.
correct_action: Check each fetch status, retry or skip the 503 page, and either exclude it from the average or surface that one source failed.
recovery_plan: Re-fetch globex.io and confirm a 200 with a non-empty body
Parse the actual Pro-tier price from the page
Recompute the average over only successfully retrieved prices
Report which sources succeeded and the corrected mean
Add a status-code and non-empty-extraction guard to the loop
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent verified HTTP 200 before extracting
Detects a default/zero value silently entering the aggregation
Asserts failed sources are excluded or flagged, not counted as 0

task: Build a cited literature summary on CRISPR off-target effects
user_request: Summarize the 2023-2024 consensus on CRISPR off-target detection methods with sources.
agent_action: Agent ran a web_search, opened the first result, and the follow-up browser.fetch on a PDF link timed out; instead of retrying it carried the search-snippet text forward and cited the PDF URL as if it had read the full paper.
failure_type: Downstream step uses a snippet after the read step failed
root_cause: The fetch of the paper PDF raised a timeout exception that was caught and swallowed; the summary step proceeded on the truncated snippet but still attached the full-paper citation.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the document was successfully retrieved because a citation URL existed. Wrong because the fetch step failed and only the snippet was in context. Avoidable by confirming the fetch returned body text before citing the source as read.
impact: Summary attributed claims to a paper the agent never actually opened, weakening the citation's reliability.
correct_action: Retry the PDF fetch (or use a reader proxy), and only cite sources whose full text was actually retrieved; mark snippet-only sources distinctly.
recovery_plan: Detect the swallowed timeout on the PDF fetch
Retry retrieval via an alternate reader or cache
Re-extract the relevant claims from the full text
Reconcile the summary against actually-read content
Downgrade or remove citations that were never opened
evaluation_criteria: Checks every cited source was actually fetched, not just listed
Detects a failed fetch being treated as a successful read
Verifies snippet-only evidence is labeled as such

task: Find and follow pagination to collect all conference speakers
user_request: List every speaker from the DevConf 2024 agenda page.
agent_action: Agent scraped page 1 of the agenda, clicked 'Next', but the click navigated to a 404 because the URL pattern changed on page 2; the agent ignored the 404 and reported only the 18 page-1 speakers as the complete list.
failure_type: Lost pagination synchronization mid-crawl
root_cause: The 'Next' link used a hashed path that returned 404; the crawl loop's exit condition was 'no error or last page', so a 404 was interpreted as 'no more pages' and the loop terminated.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a non-OK response on Next meant the end of pagination. Wrong because it was a broken link, not the final page (the footer showed 'Page 1 of 4'). Avoidable by reading the pager's total-page count and asserting collected pages matched it.
impact: User got 18 of ~70 speakers and assumed the list was complete, missing three-quarters of the agenda.
correct_action: Detect the 404, resolve the correct page-2 URL from the pager control, and continue until the page counter is exhausted.
recovery_plan: Compare collected page count against the pager's 'X of N' total
Re-derive the correct next-page URL pattern
Resume crawling from page 2 through page 4
Deduplicate and assemble the full speaker list
Add a completeness assertion against the page total
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent validated total expected pages vs collected
Detects a 404 misread as end-of-pagination
Asserts final result completeness was verified

task: Verify a claimed statistic across multiple sources
user_request: Confirm whether global EV sales crossed 14 million units in 2023 and cite two independent sources.
agent_action: Agent's first source confirmed 14M; the second web_search returned zero results due to a malformed query, but the agent reported 'two sources confirm' and fabricated agreement from the single source.
failure_type: Proceeds after an intermediate search returns empty
root_cause: The second search step returned an empty result set (the query string had an unescaped operator), and the verification step proceeded as though a second corroborating source existed.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the two-source verification chain completed successfully. Wrong because the second search yielded nothing and was never re-run. Avoidable by asserting result_count>0 on the second search before claiming corroboration.
impact: User was told two independent sources agreed when only one was actually consulted, overstating confidence.
correct_action: Detect the empty second-search result, reformulate the query, and only claim corroboration once a genuinely independent source confirms.
recovery_plan: Notice the second search returned zero results
Reformulate the query with proper escaping
Retrieve and read a genuinely independent second source
Compare both figures explicitly
Report the verification with both real citations
evaluation_criteria: Checks the second source was actually retrieved before corroboration claim
Detects empty search results treated as success
Verifies two distinct sources were cited

task: Re-embed updated documents into the vector index
user_request: Re-index the 12 updated policy PDFs into our Pinecone namespace so search picks up the changes.
agent_action: Agent chunked and called the embeddings API, but 4 of 12 chunked files returned a 429 rate-limit on embedding; the agent still ran pinecone.upsert for the 8 that succeeded and reported 'all 12 re-indexed'.
failure_type: Partial batch failure reported as full success
root_cause: The embed step returned 429 for 4 files; those vectors were never produced, but the upsert+report step counted intended files rather than successfully embedded ones.
why_it_failed: Assumption: every file in the batch got an embedding before upsert. Wrong because 4 hit a rate limit and were silently dropped. Avoidable by asserting embedding_count==file_count and retrying the 429s with backoff before reporting.
impact: Search continued returning stale text for 4 policies; users got outdated answers with no error surfaced.
correct_action: Retry the 429 files with exponential backoff, confirm all 12 produced vectors, then upsert and verify index vector count.
recovery_plan: Diff the namespace vector count against expected 12 docs
Identify the 4 files missing embeddings
Re-embed them with backoff on 429
Upsert the missing vectors
Verify retrieval returns the updated text for all 12
evaluation_criteria: Checks embedding success count equals file count before upsert
Detects 429 responses ignored in a batch
Asserts a post-upsert index count verification

task: Answer a question using retrieval-augmented generation
user_request: What is our refund window per the latest customer policy doc?
agent_action: Agent's retrieval step (pinecone.query) returned an error 'dimension mismatch 768 vs 1536'; the agent caught it, retrieved nothing, and answered '30 days' from general knowledge instead of the document.
failure_type: Retrieval error swallowed, answer from priors
root_cause: The query embedding used a 1536-dim model while the index was built at 768; pinecone.query raised a dimension-mismatch error that was caught, and the generation step ran with empty context.
why_it_failed: Assumption: retrieval succeeded and context was present. Wrong because the query vector dimension didn't match the index, so zero passages were retrieved. Avoidable by failing closed when retrieved_passages is empty instead of answering ungrounded.
impact: User received an unsourced refund window (actual policy was 14 days), risking a wrong customer commitment.
correct_action: Surface the dimension mismatch, re-embed the query with the index's model, retrieve the actual passage, and answer only from it.
recovery_plan: Detect the dimension-mismatch error from pinecone.query
Re-embed the query with the 768-dim model matching the index
Retrieve the policy passage and confirm non-empty context
Answer strictly from the retrieved text with citation
Add a guard that blocks generation on empty retrieval
evaluation_criteria: Checks generation is blocked when retrieval returns empty/error
Detects an answer grounded in priors after a retrieval failure
Verifies query and index embedding dimensions match

task: Chunk and ingest a large manual into the RAG store
user_request: Ingest the 400-page hardware manual into our Weaviate class so support can search it.
agent_action: Agent split the PDF into 1,100 chunks and looped weaviate.data.create; around chunk 640 the client connection dropped, the loop's try/except logged and continued, and the agent reported 'ingestion complete' with only 638 objects stored.
failure_type: Mid-loop connection drop swallowed by try/except
root_cause: A transient WebSocket disconnect threw on inserts 639-1100; the broad except clause logged each and continued, so the loop finished 'successfully' with 462 chunks never written.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the loop completing means all chunks were stored. Wrong because a mid-run disconnect dropped 462 inserts that were only logged, not retried. Avoidable by comparing stored object count to chunk count after the loop.
impact: Roughly 40% of the manual (later sections) was unsearchable; support agents got 'not found' for valid topics.
correct_action: Track per-chunk insert success, reconnect and retry failures, and assert stored count equals chunk count before declaring completion.
recovery_plan: Count objects in the Weaviate class vs expected 1,100
Identify the chunk ID range that failed (639-1100)
Reconnect and re-insert the missing chunks idempotently
Verify the final object count matches
Replace the swallow-and-continue with retry-and-assert logic
evaluation_criteria: Checks stored count is reconciled with intended chunk count
Detects exceptions swallowed mid-loop without retry
Asserts a completeness check before reporting success

task: Hybrid search then rerank for a support query
user_request: Find the top passage about resetting the device to factory defaults.
agent_action: Agent ran the vector search, then called the cohere.rerank step which returned a 400 'documents list empty'; the agent ignored the 400 and returned the unreranked top hit, which was about a software reset, not factory reset.
failure_type: Rerank error ignored, raw results passed through
root_cause: The rerank call failed with 400 because the documents payload was truncated by a serialization bug; the pipeline fell through to the pre-rerank ordering without flagging that reranking never ran.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the returned passage was the reranked best match. Wrong because rerank 400'd and the raw vector order (a near-duplicate topic) was served. Avoidable by checking the rerank response status and asserting reranked_results is non-empty before selecting top-1.
impact: User got instructions for a software reset instead of a factory reset, a subtly wrong but plausible answer.
correct_action: Detect the 400, fix the documents payload, re-run rerank, and select the top passage only from a successful rerank response.
recovery_plan: Notice the rerank call returned 400, not results
Fix the document serialization passed to rerank
Re-run rerank on the candidate passages
Select top-1 from the reranked set
Add a non-empty rerank-output assertion
evaluation_criteria: Checks the reranked output was non-empty before selection
Detects a rerank 400 silently bypassed
Verifies the served passage came from the rerank step

task: Backfill metadata filters on retrieved chunks
user_request: Answer using only chunks tagged product='X200' from the index.
agent_action: Agent issued pinecone.query with a metadata filter, but the filter key was mistyped as 'prod' (not 'product'); Pinecone returned 0 matches, the agent retried once with the same typo, got 0 again, then answered from unfiltered top hits.
failure_type: Filtered step yields empty, falls back to unfiltered
root_cause: The metadata filter {'prod':'X200'} matched no vectors because the indexed key is 'product'; after two empty results the pipeline dropped the filter rather than fixing the key.
why_it_failed: Assumption: empty filtered results meant no X200 chunks exist, so unfiltered is acceptable. Wrong because the filter key was misspelled; X200 chunks did exist. Avoidable by validating the filter key against index metadata schema before falling back.
impact: Answer mixed in chunks from other products (X100, X300), producing a partially incorrect spec answer.
correct_action: Validate the metadata key against the index schema, correct it to 'product', and re-query before considering any fallback.
recovery_plan: Inspect index metadata schema for the correct key name
Re-issue the query with filter {'product':'X200'}
Confirm matches are returned for X200
Regenerate the answer from correctly filtered chunks
Reject unfiltered fallback when a filter was required
evaluation_criteria: Checks the filter key was validated before fallback
Detects an unfiltered fallback after a required filter returned empty
Asserts answer chunks all match the required tag

task: Copy a shared folder of reports into an archive folder
user_request: Move all 23 files from 'Q1 Reports' into the 'Archive/2024' Drive folder.
agent_action: Agent listed 23 files and looped gdrive.files.update to set the new parent; file #9 failed with 403 (it was owned by another user), the agent didn't stop, and reported '23 files moved' while 9 onward never moved.
failure_type: Per-item 403 in a move loop ignored
root_cause: gdrive.files.update on a file owned by another user returned 403 insufficientPermissions; the loop caught nothing, the error response was discarded, and the success count reflected list length not move successes.
why_it_failed: Assumption: each update call succeeded because the loop didn't throw. Wrong because the API returned 403 in the body for non-owned files. Avoidable by checking each response for an error field and reconciling moved count against listed count.
impact: 15 files remained in the source folder; a later cleanup deleted 'Q1 Reports' assuming it was empty, risking loss of unmoved files.
correct_action: Inspect each move response, request ownership/permission for 403 files or report them, and verify the destination contains all 23 before declaring done.
recovery_plan: List the destination 'Archive/2024' and count moved files
Identify the files still in 'Q1 Reports'
Resolve permissions or transfer ownership for 403 items
Re-run the move for the remaining files
Verify source is empty only after destination has all 23
evaluation_criteria: Checks each move response was inspected for errors
Detects a 403 item counted as moved
Asserts destination completeness before source cleanup

task: Generate and share an export of a Google Doc
user_request: Export the 'Roadmap' doc to PDF and share the PDF link with the team.
agent_action: Agent called gdrive.files.export which returned a 'export size limit exceeded' error for the large doc; the agent then shared the original Doc's edit link instead, and told the user 'PDF shared' though no PDF was created.
failure_type: Export failed, mislabeled fallback as the deliverable
root_cause: The export step hit the 10MB export cap and returned an error; the subsequent share step ran against the original Doc file ID and was reported as the PDF that never existed.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a shareable link existed for a PDF. Wrong because export failed and the link pointed to the editable Doc, not a PDF. Avoidable by confirming export returned binary content and a PDF file ID before sharing it as 'the PDF'.
impact: Team received an editable Doc with comment access instead of a frozen PDF, and one member edited the live roadmap by accident.
correct_action: Handle the export size error (export per-section or via Drive's PDF conversion), confirm a PDF file was produced, then share that file.
recovery_plan: Detect the export-size error from gdrive.files.export
Produce the PDF via a supported path (split or print-to-Drive)
Confirm a distinct PDF file ID now exists
Share that PDF file with view-only permission
Correct the earlier message that claimed a PDF was shared
evaluation_criteria: Checks a PDF artifact was actually produced before sharing
Detects an export error masked by sharing the source doc
Verifies the shared link type matches what was promised

task: Find a file by name and append a row of data to it
user_request: Append today's signups (1,204) to the 'Daily Metrics' sheet.
agent_action: Agent ran gdrive.files.list with q name='Daily Metrics' which returned two files (an old archived copy first); the agent appended to the first result, the archived 2023 sheet, instead of the active one.
failure_type: Ambiguous lookup result feeds wrong ID downstream
root_cause: The list step returned 2 matches; the agent took files[0] without disambiguating by parent folder or modifiedTime, passing the stale file ID into the sheets.values.append step.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the name search returned a single, correct file. Wrong because two files shared the name and the archived one sorted first. Avoidable by checking result count and selecting by folder/most-recent modifiedTime, or asking which file.
impact: Today's metric landed in a dead archive sheet; the live dashboard showed no signups for the day.
correct_action: Detect the multi-match, disambiguate by parent folder and modifiedTime (or confirm with the user), then append to the active sheet only.
recovery_plan: Re-list and observe more than one name match
Identify the active sheet by folder and recent modifiedTime
Remove the row mistakenly appended to the archive
Append the value to the correct active sheet
Add disambiguation when a lookup returns multiple files
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent handled multiple lookup matches
Detects files[0] used without disambiguation
Verifies the write targeted the active, correct file

task: Watch a folder and process newly uploaded CSVs
user_request: For each new CSV in 'Inbox', parse it and add a summary row to the 'Index' sheet.
agent_action: Agent paged gdrive.files.list but used only the first page (pageSize 10) and never followed nextPageToken; 7 newer CSVs on page 2 were never processed, and the agent reported 'all new files processed'.
failure_type: Pagination cursor dropped between steps
root_cause: The list response included a nextPageToken indicating more results, but the processing loop iterated only the first page and discarded the token, so 7 files were never fed downstream.
why_it_failed: Assumption: one list call returned every new file. Wrong because the result was paginated and a nextPageToken was present. Avoidable by looping until nextPageToken is absent before processing.
impact: 7 customer CSVs went unprocessed; their metrics were missing from the index for the day with no error.
correct_action: Follow nextPageToken until exhausted to assemble the full file list, then process every file.
recovery_plan: Re-list following nextPageToken to enumerate all files
Diff processed file IDs against the full set
Process the 7 missed CSVs
Append their summary rows to the Index sheet
Add a loop that drains pagination before processing
evaluation_criteria: Checks pagination was fully drained before processing
Detects nextPageToken ignored
Asserts processed count equals total new-file count

task: Read attachments from an email and save them to Drive
user_request: Grab the invoice PDFs from the latest email from billing@vendor.com and put them in 'Invoices'.
agent_action: Agent called gmail.messages.get with format='metadata', which returns no attachment bytes; it then 'saved' files using the attachment filenames but zero-byte content, creating 3 empty PDFs in Drive.
failure_type: Wrong intermediate format yields no payload downstream
root_cause: format='metadata' returns headers only, no body/attachment data; the download step received no attachmentId payload and wrote empty files, but the create step succeeded so it looked done.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the message fetch included attachment content. Wrong because metadata format omits bodies; a second gmail.attachments.get call was required. Avoidable by checking attachment byte size > 0 before writing to Drive.
impact: Three 0-byte 'invoices' were saved; accounting opened blank PDFs and the real invoices were never archived.
correct_action: Fetch the message with full format, extract each attachmentId, call gmail.attachments.get for the bytes, and verify non-zero size before saving.
recovery_plan: Detect the saved PDFs are 0 bytes
Re-fetch the message with format='full'
Download each attachment via gmail.attachments.get
Confirm byte size > 0 and valid PDF header
Overwrite the empty Drive files with real content
evaluation_criteria: Checks attachment bytes were fetched, not just metadata
Detects 0-byte files written downstream
Asserts file size validation before save

task: Send a templated follow-up to a list of leads
user_request: Send the follow-up template to all 14 leads in this thread and confirm.
agent_action: Agent built drafts then called gmail.messages.send in a loop; send #6 returned 429 'rate limit', the loop continued, and the agent reported 'all 14 sent' though sends 6-14 silently failed.
failure_type: Send-loop rate limit ignored, count overstated
root_cause: A 429 with Retry-After was returned on the 6th send; the loop neither honored Retry-After nor recorded failures, so 9 leads never received the email but were counted as sent.
why_it_failed: Assumption: each send call delivered because the loop finished. Wrong because Gmail rate-limited after 5 rapid sends. Avoidable by checking each send's status and honoring Retry-After, then reconciling sent IDs to the lead list.
impact: 9 of 14 leads got no follow-up while the user believed the campaign completed, causing missed conversions.
correct_action: Honor Retry-After with backoff, retry the failed sends, and confirm a message ID per lead before reporting completion.
recovery_plan: List actually-sent message IDs and compare to the 14 leads
Identify leads 6-14 with no sent message
Re-send with backoff honoring Retry-After
Confirm a returned message ID for each lead
Report the true delivered count
evaluation_criteria: Checks each send returned a message ID before counting it
Detects 429 responses ignored in the loop
Asserts Retry-After/backoff was honored

task: Label and archive a search result set of emails
user_request: Find all emails from noreply@alerts.io older than 90 days, label them 'Old Alerts', and archive them.
agent_action: Agent ran gmail.messages.list with the query, applied the label in a batch modify, but the modify response listed several message IDs under 'failures'; the agent skipped to archiving and removed INBOX from messages that were never labeled.
failure_type: Batch step partial failure not reconciled before next step
root_cause: gmail.users.messages.batchModify returned a partial-success payload with some IDs failing the addLabel; the agent proceeded to removeLabelIds INBOX on the full set, decoupling labeling from archiving.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the batch label applied to every message before archiving. Wrong because the response flagged per-message failures. Avoidable by reading the batch response's failures and only archiving messages confirmed labeled.
impact: Several alerts were archived without the 'Old Alerts' label, making them unfindable by the intended filter.
correct_action: Parse the batch-modify response, retry the failed label additions, and archive only messages confirmed to carry the label.
recovery_plan: Read the batchModify response and list failed IDs
Re-apply the 'Old Alerts' label to those IDs
Confirm all target messages now carry the label
Archive only the confirmed-labeled set
Re-label and re-find any prematurely archived messages
evaluation_criteria: Checks the batch response failures were parsed
Detects archiving decoupled from confirmed labeling
Asserts each archived message carries the label

task: Thread a reply onto an existing email conversation
user_request: Reply to the customer's last email in the 'Order 8841' thread saying we shipped it.
agent_action: Agent called gmail.threads.get to fetch the thread but got a 404 (the thread ID was from a prior stale session); it then sent a brand-new email without threadId or In-Reply-To headers, starting a disconnected conversation.
failure_type: Missing-thread error not handled, downstream send orphaned
root_cause: threads.get returned 404 for a stale thread ID; instead of re-resolving the thread, the send step ran with no threadId/References, so the reply did not attach to the conversation.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the thread existed and the reply would attach. Wrong because the thread ID was stale and the get failed. Avoidable by re-searching for the live thread on a 404 and including threadId and References on send.
impact: Customer received a context-less email; the original thread showed no reply, confusing the support handoff.
correct_action: On 404, search the mailbox for the current 'Order 8841' thread, then send the reply with the correct threadId and References headers.
recovery_plan: Detect the 404 from threads.get
Search for the live thread by subject/order ID
Build the reply with threadId and References set
Send and confirm it appears in the existing thread
Avoid sending orphaned messages on lookup failure
evaluation_criteria: Checks a 404 triggered re-resolution of the thread
Detects a reply sent without threading headers
Verifies the reply attached to the existing thread

task: Run a dependency CVE scan and open issues for criticals
user_request: Scan our repo's dependencies and file a GitHub issue for each critical CVE.
agent_action: Agent ran 'npm audit --json' but the process exited code 1 (which npm uses when vulns are found); the agent treated exit!=0 as 'scan failed', skipped parsing, and reported 'no issues filed, scan errored'.
failure_type: Tool exit code misread, downstream parsing skipped
root_cause: npm audit exits non-zero when vulnerabilities exist; the agent's success gate required exit code 0, so valid JSON on stdout was never parsed and no issues were created.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a non-zero exit meant the scan failed. Wrong because npm audit returns 1 precisely when it finds vulnerabilities. Avoidable by parsing stdout JSON regardless of exit code, or treating exit codes 0/1 as success per npm's documented behavior.
impact: 7 critical CVEs went unticketed; the team believed the scan errored and dependencies stayed vulnerable.
correct_action: Parse the JSON on stdout even when exit code is 1, extract critical advisories, and open an issue per CVE.
recovery_plan: Re-run 'npm audit --json' and capture stdout regardless of exit
Parse advisories and filter severity=critical
Create a GitHub issue per critical CVE
Verify issue count matches critical-CVE count
Treat npm audit exit code 1 as 'vulns found', not failure
evaluation_criteria: Checks stdout JSON was parsed despite non-zero exit
Detects npm audit exit 1 misread as failure
Asserts an issue was filed per critical CVE

task: Run SAST and post a summary comment on the PR
user_request: Run Semgrep on PR #2207 and comment a summary of findings.
agent_action: Agent ran semgrep with a ruleset that 404'd on fetch ('p/owasp-top-ten' typo'd as 'p/owsap'); semgrep printed 0 findings due to no rules loaded, and the agent commented 'No security issues found' on the PR.
failure_type: Empty result from a failed config step read as 'clean'
root_cause: The ruleset registry fetch failed (misspelled config slug), so semgrep ran with no rules and emitted zero findings; the comment step interpreted zero findings as a passing scan.
why_it_failed: Assumption: 0 findings meant the code was clean. Wrong because no rules were loaded, so nothing could be found. Avoidable by asserting rules_loaded>0 (semgrep prints rule count) before treating zero findings as a clean result.
impact: A real SQL-injection pattern in the PR went unflagged and the PR was approved on a falsely-clean scan.
correct_action: Verify the ruleset loaded (non-zero rule count) before interpreting results; fix the slug, re-run, and only then summarize findings.
recovery_plan: Check semgrep output for rules-loaded count
Correct the ruleset slug to 'p/owasp-top-ten'
Re-run Semgrep on PR #2207
Confirm rules loaded and review real findings
Comment the accurate summary; never equate no-rules with clean
evaluation_criteria: Checks rules-loaded count was verified before reporting clean
Detects a failed ruleset fetch yielding false 'no issues'
Asserts the scan actually executed rules against the diff

task: Gate a release on a container image vulnerability scan
user_request: Scan the release image with Trivy and block the deploy if there are any criticals.
agent_action: Agent ran 'trivy image app:2.7.0' but the DB download step hit a network timeout and Trivy skipped scanning with a warning; the agent saw an empty vuln list, called it 'no criticals', and let the deploy proceed.
failure_type: Skipped scan (stale/no DB) treated as a passing gate
root_cause: Trivy's vulnerability DB fetch timed out; it emitted a warning and produced an empty results array, which the gate logic read as zero criticals and allowed the release.
why_it_failed: Assumption: an empty results array meant no vulnerabilities. Wrong because the DB never loaded, so no scanning occurred. Avoidable by checking Trivy's exit/warning for DB-download failure and failing the gate when the scan didn't actually run.
impact: An image with a known critical OpenSSL CVE shipped to production because the gate passed on a non-scan.
correct_action: Treat a failed DB download as a scan failure (block the deploy), retry with cached DB, and only pass the gate on a successful scan reporting zero criticals.
recovery_plan: Detect the Trivy DB-download warning/timeout
Retry the scan with --skip-db-update against a cached DB
Confirm the scan actually ran (non-empty findings metadata)
Re-evaluate the critical gate on real results
Roll back the deploy if a critical is present
evaluation_criteria: Checks the gate distinguishes 'scan failed' from 'no vulns'
Detects an empty DB-less result passing the gate
Asserts the scan ran before allowing deploy

task: Patch a vulnerable dependency and verify the fix
user_request: Bump lodash to a non-vulnerable version and confirm the CVE is resolved.
agent_action: Agent edited package.json to lodash ^4.17.21 but never ran 'npm install'; the lockfile and node_modules still pinned 4.17.15, yet the agent re-ran audit against the unchanged tree and reported 'CVE resolved'.
failure_type: Skipped install step, verification ran on stale state
root_cause: The dependency bump only changed package.json; without npm install, package-lock.json and the installed tree kept the vulnerable 4.17.15, so the re-audit reflected the old state.
why_it_failed: Assumption: editing package.json updated the resolved dependency. Wrong because the lockfile/install drives the actual version and was never refreshed. Avoidable by running npm install and verifying the lockfile resolved version before re-auditing.
impact: The CVE remained present in the shipped build while the team believed it was patched.
correct_action: Run npm install to update the lockfile, confirm package-lock pins 4.17.21, then re-run the audit against the updated tree.
recovery_plan: Check package-lock.json for the resolved lodash version
Run npm install to refresh the lockfile and node_modules
Confirm 4.17.21 is now resolved
Re-run npm audit and confirm the CVE is gone
Make verification depend on the installed tree, not package.json
evaluation_criteria: Checks the lockfile was updated before re-auditing
Detects verification run against a stale install
Asserts the resolved version changed, not just the manifest

task: Refund a customer charge and email confirmation
user_request: Refund charge ch_3PQ for $50 to the customer and email them a confirmation.
agent_action: Agent called stripe.refunds.create which returned status 'pending' (not 'succeeded') for the bank rail; the agent immediately sent 'Your $50 refund is complete' without waiting for or checking the final refund status.
failure_type: Acted on a non-final intermediate status
root_cause: The refund object returned status='pending'; the confirmation step keyed off 'a refund object was returned' rather than status=='succeeded', sending a premature 'complete' message.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a returned refund object meant the refund completed. Wrong because ACH refunds settle asynchronously and start as 'pending', sometimes failing. Avoidable by checking refund.status or subscribing to the refund.updated webhook before confirming.
impact: The refund later failed for insufficient funds on the source; the customer had been told it was done, causing a dispute.
correct_action: Send confirmation only after refund.status reaches 'succeeded', via polling stripe.refunds.retrieve or the refund.updated webhook; otherwise communicate 'pending'.
recovery_plan: Retrieve the refund and read its current status
If failed, re-initiate or escalate the refund
Wait for status='succeeded' before any 'complete' message
Send an accurate status update to the customer
Gate confirmation emails on terminal refund status
evaluation_criteria: Checks confirmation waited for terminal refund status
Detects 'pending' treated as 'succeeded'
Asserts status was re-read before emailing

task: Create a subscription with a coupon for a new customer
user_request: Subscribe cus_Oa42 to the Pro plan and apply the LAUNCH20 coupon.
agent_action: Agent created the subscription first, then called stripe.subscriptions.update to attach the coupon, but the update returned 'coupon expired'; the agent ignored the error and reported 'subscribed with 20% off', leaving the customer on full price.
failure_type: Second-step failure ignored, success overstated
root_cause: The coupon-attach update failed with 'No such coupon / expired'; the subscription was already active at full price, but the report claimed the discount applied because the create step had succeeded.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the discount applied because the subscription was created. Wrong because the coupon attach was a separate call that failed. Avoidable by checking the update response and verifying subscription.discount is set before reporting the discounted price.
impact: Customer was billed full price despite being promised 20% off, risking a chargeback and trust loss.
correct_action: Validate the coupon first, attach it at subscription creation, and confirm subscription.discount is present before reporting the price.
recovery_plan: Retrieve the subscription and check the discount field
Validate or substitute a current equivalent coupon
Apply the working coupon to the subscription
Confirm the discount now appears on the next invoice
Report only after the discount is verified
evaluation_criteria: Checks the coupon-attach response was inspected
Detects an expired-coupon error reported as success
Asserts subscription.discount was verified

task: Migrate customers to a new price and invoice them
user_request: Move the 30 customers on price_old to price_new and generate their next invoices.
agent_action: Agent looped stripe.subscriptions.update across 30 subs; on customer 12 the call returned a 402 (card declined on proration), the loop continued, and the agent generated invoices for all 30 assuming the price change stuck for everyone.
failure_type: Mid-batch payment error desynchronizes later steps
root_cause: A 402 on the proration charge for sub_12 left that subscription unmodified, but the loop didn't record the failure; the invoice-generation step ran over all 30 including ones still on price_old.
why_it_failed: Assumption: every subscription moved to price_new before invoicing. Wrong because a declined proration left some on the old price. Avoidable by collecting per-update results and invoicing only confirmed-migrated subscriptions.
impact: Several customers were invoiced at the old price or with proration mismatches, requiring manual credit notes to fix.
correct_action: Record each update's result, retry or flag 402s, and invoice only subscriptions confirmed on price_new.
recovery_plan: List subscriptions still on price_old after the loop
Resolve the declined proration for those customers
Re-apply the price change once payment clears
Verify all 30 are on price_new
Generate invoices only for confirmed-migrated subs
evaluation_criteria: Checks per-subscription update results were reconciled
Detects a 402 ignored mid-batch
Asserts invoicing targeted only migrated subscriptions

task: Charge a customer after creating a payment intent
user_request: Charge cus_9Lp $120 for the annual plan using their saved card.
agent_action: Agent created a PaymentIntent that returned status 'requires_action' (3DS needed); the agent skipped the confirmation/authentication step, marked the order 'paid' in the DB, and provisioned the annual plan.
failure_type: Skipped a required intermediate auth step in the chain
root_cause: The PaymentIntent came back as 'requires_action' for 3D Secure; the order-fulfillment step ran on 'an intent was created' rather than status=='succeeded', so provisioning happened without an actual capture.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating the PaymentIntent captured the funds. Wrong because the intent needed 3DS authentication and no money moved. Avoidable by gating fulfillment on PaymentIntent.status=='succeeded' after handling requires_action.
impact: The customer received a paid annual plan while no payment was captured, a direct revenue loss until reconciliation caught it.
correct_action: Handle 'requires_action' (return the client_secret for 3DS), and provision only after the PaymentIntent reaches 'succeeded'.
recovery_plan: Retrieve the PaymentIntent and read its real status
Complete 3DS authentication or request a new payment method
Confirm status reaches 'succeeded' and funds captured
Only then mark the order paid and keep provisioning
Reverse provisioning if payment ultimately fails
evaluation_criteria: Checks fulfillment waited for status='succeeded'
Detects 'requires_action' treated as paid
Asserts 3DS authentication was handled before provisioning
